title: The scalar localization of a linear category is a linear category
statement: Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $\varpi\in R$, $R[1/\varpi]$ the localization of $R$ at $\varpi$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away], and $\mathcal C$ an $R$-linear category [def-weil-linear-category]. For objects $K,L$ put $H(K,L)=\Hom_{\mathcal C}(K,L)\otimes_RR[1/\varpi]$, the base change of the $R$-module $\Hom_{\mathcal C}(K,L)$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. Then: (1) for objects $K,L,M$ there is a unique $R[1/\varpi]$-bilinear map $\circ:H(L,M)\times H(K,L)\to H(K,M)$ with $(f\otimes a)\circ(g\otimes b)=(f\circ g)\otimes ab$; (2) this composition is associative and $\mathrm{id}_K\otimes1$ is a two-sided identity, so the objects of $\mathcal C$ with the $R[1/\varpi]$-modules $H(K,L)$ form an $R[1/\varpi]$-linear category $\mathcal C[1/\varpi]$; (3) $Q:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C[1/\varpi]$, identity on objects and $f\mapsto f\otimes1$ on morphisms, is a functor and is $R$-linear [def-weil-linear-functor] for the $R$-linear structure of $\mathcal C[1/\varpi]$ obtained by restriction of scalars along $R\to R[1/\varpi]$; (4) if $T:\mathcal C\to\mathcal C$ is an automorphism of categories that is $R$-linear, then $K\mapsto T(K)$, $f\otimes a\mapsto T(f)\otimes a$ is a well-defined $R[1/\varpi]$-linear automorphism $T'$ of $\mathcal C[1/\varpi]$ (with inverse induced by $T^{-1}$), and $Q\circ T=T'\circ Q$.
